title: Call chain: DELETE /orders/{id}

side_effects: Set in-request tenant context from X-Tenant-Id / X-User-Id headers
Validate order exists and belongs to current tenant
Soft-delete order row (deleted=true, status=cancelled) in orders table
Clear tenant context after handler completes

raw_content:
Tracing DELETE `/orders/{id}` through the codebase — I'll map the handler chain and any durable side effects.
DELETE `/orders/{id}` is handled by `handle_delete_order`, which authenticates, delegates to `cancel_order` (soft-delete + outbox + cache), then clears auth. `legacy_order.py` is explicitly decoy code and not on this path.

  "chain": [
    "api.orders.handle_delete_order",
    "pkg.auth.authenticate",
    "pkg.tenant.set_tenant",
    "service.order_service.cancel_order",
    "pkg.tenant.require_tenant",
    "store.order_repo.get",
    "store.order_repo.soft_delete",
    "store.db.put",
    "pkg.events.order_cancelled",
    "store.outbox.insert",
    "store.db.put",
    "store.cache.invalidate_order",
    "pkg.auth.clear_auth",
    "pkg.tenant.set_tenant"
  ],
  "side_effects": [
    "Set in-request tenant context from X-Tenant-Id / X-User-Id headers",
    "Validate order exists and belongs to current tenant",

    "Insert OrderCancelled outbox row (acked=false, published=false)",
    "Remove order:{id} from in-memory cache",
